title: Demystifying MDR: UPI vs. Debit and Credit Card Charges
description: Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) is a fee merchants pay to banks and payment processors for accepting digital payments. The National Payments Corporation of India.

faq.a: MDR, or Merchant Discount Rate, is a fee charged to merchants by banks and payment service providers for processing digital transactions made by customers using instruments like credit cards, debit cards, or UPI.

faq.q: Will consumers pay MDR for UPI transactions?
faq.a: No, consumers will continue to use UPI free of cost. The MDR is a charge applicable only to merchants for accepting certain Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI payments.
MDR of 0.4% applies to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000. For transactions of ₹75,000 and above, the MDR is capped at ₹300.

faq.q: Are small merchants affected by UPI MDR?
faq.a: Small merchants operating under the P2PM framework, receiving up to ₹1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes into their personal accounts, are exempt from MDR.

faq.q: How does UPI MDR compare to credit card MDR?
faq.a: UPI MDR (0.4%, capped at ₹300 for high values) is significantly lower than standard credit card MDRs, which typically range from 1.5% to 2.5% per transaction.

faq.q: What happens if I use a credit card linked to UPI?
faq.a: Transactions made using a credit card linked to UPI (e.g., RuPay credit cards) will follow the MDR rules applicable to the underlying credit product, not the new 0.4% UPI MDR framework.

faq.q: Can merchants pass UPI MDR charges to customers?
faq.a: No, merchants are strictly prohibited from passing on MDR charges to customers while accepting payments through UPI. Consumers must only pay the posted price.

based_on.title: How does MDR on UPI compare to charges on traditional debit and credit cards? Here's what NCPI's FAQs say…
